name: The Hope Standard
headline: The standard we hold ourselves to. The standard we believe everyone should meet.
intro: We do not treat ethics as a feature. It is the foundation of every line of code we write. Every product we release is designed, tested, and audited against The Hope Standard, our framework for responsible AI, before it reaches a single user.
closing: We publish how we build because we want the rest of the industry to build this way too.

pillars.title: Privacy by design
pillars.statement: We collect only what is needed, protect it rigorously, and never sell it.
pillars.check: Before we build, we write a data inventory: every field, why it exists, who can see it, and when it is deleted. If a field has no reason, it is cut.
pillars.see: A plain-language data page for every product, explaining what is collected and what is not.

pillars.title: Algorithmic auditing
pillars.statement: We test how our systems make decisions and document what we find.
pillars.check: Decisions the system makes are logged. We sample them, review them by hand, and write down what we learned, including the surprises.
pillars.see: An audit summary you can actually read, not a certificate.

pillars.title: Bias testing
pillars.statement: We examine our models and data for unfair outcomes before and after launch.
pillars.check: Outcomes are compared across groups before release and on a schedule afterward. If a gap appears, the fix ships before the feature does.
pillars.see: What we tested, what we found, and what we changed.

pillars.title: Transparency
pillars.statement: Users know when AI is involved and how it reaches its answers.
pillars.check: Anything generated or ranked by AI is labeled, shows its sources, and says how confident it is. No quiet automation.
pillars.see: An "AI-assisted" label and citations right in the product.

pillars.title: Human judgment leads
pillars.check: No final decision about a person's money, housing, health, or job is automated. A human can always override, and a human's name is on it.
pillars.see: A person's name on every recommendation that matters.
